title: Use Drilldown to investigate without a query

blocks.content:
Picture this. You run an online store, and this morning checkout is twice as slow as usual. No dashboard covers checkout latency, because nobody predicted this problem. Dashboards show what someone already thought to watch. When the question is new, you need a way to investigate.

That's what Drilldown is for. Start from one of the signals, click filters, and narrow down until you've found what changed, all without writing a query. In this guide you'll practice that kind of investigation. The data here comes from a demo system rather than a store, but the moves are the same ones you'd use on your own Grafana Cloud data.
First, open Drilldown and see where an investigation starts.

Click **Drilldown** in the main menu.

The page that opens offers four starting points, one for each signal your systems produce. Those are **Metrics**, **Logs**, **Traces**, and **Profiles**.

Click **Metrics**.

Metrics are numbers recorded over time, and a slow checkout is a number. Every metric appears as a chart before you ask for anything, so you start with everything on the table.
You started with Metrics, and Drilldown showed every metric it has. No query written.
Next, narrow the view from everything down to the one thing that changed.

Click **Select** on the first metric.

In a real investigation you'd pick the metric that tracks checkout latency. The view narrows to that one metric, broken down by its labels.
blocks.tooltip: One click narrows from everything to one thing, and the breakdown that opens splits it further with one chart per label.

blocks.content:
Notice the filter field.

Pick a label and a value, and every chart narrows to match. Each pick asks a question. Is it one server? One region? Clicking filters is the whole workflow.
blocks.tooltip: Each pick narrows the result, and a few stacked together identify the problem without writing a query.

blocks.content:
Find the **Related logs** tab.

A spike in the numbers often has a matching error in the logs. This tab jumps from the metric you're watching straight to those text records, so you keep going without starting over.
blocks.tooltip: One click carries the investigation from the numbers to the matching text records.

blocks.content: Start from everything, narrow with clicks, jump to the matching logs. That's an investigation in Grafana Cloud, and you never wrote a query. When you uncover something worth watching from then on, that's when someone builds a dashboard, and the [guide on dashboards](https://interactive-learning.grafana.net/guides/get-started-see-dashboards) shows you how to read one.
